candidates.evidence: G at 1581 cm-1 (FWHM ~14), single symmetric Lorentzian 2D at 2699 cm-1 (FWHM ~32), I2D/IG ≈ 2.7–3 (peak height); weak D at 1347.8 cm-1.
2D would be broader (~50+ cm-1) and multi-component with I2D/IG ≲ 1; not seen.
Can give a single Lorentzian 2D, but 2D FWHM ~32 and high I2D/IG favour a monolayer.

hint_reasoning: No material hint was given. The task was identification from the spectrum alone.

peaks.assignment: D band (defect-activated breathing mode, near-K TO phonon)
peaks.source: Lorentzian fit of the spectrum; assignment per Ferrari & Basko, Nat. Nanotechnol. 8, 235 (2013)

peaks.assignment: G band (in-plane C–C stretch, zone-centre LO/TO)
peaks.source: Lorentzian fit of the spectrum; Ferrari et al., PRL 97, 187401 (2006)

peaks.assignment: 2D band (second-order D, double resonance), single Lorentzian
peaks.source: Lorentzian fit of the spectrum; Ferrari et al., PRL 97, 187401 (2006)
Expected Si first-order line. It lies outside the measured window (1100–3000 cm-1), so it was not observed.

properties.name: layers
properties.source: Single-Lorentzian 2D with FWHM ~32 cm-1 and I2D/IG ≈ 2.7–3 (Ferrari 2006; Ni et al., Nano Lett. 8, 2008)

properties.name: defect_level
properties.source: ID/IG ≈ 0.16 (height ratio) or 0.17 (area ratio), stage-1 regime (Cançado et al., Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (2011))

properties.name: L_D_nm
properties.source: Cançado 2011: L_D² = 1.8e-9·λ⁴·(IG/ID) nm², with λ = 532 nm and IG/ID ≈ 5.9 (area ratio). This is valid only for point-like defects in the low-defect regime. The equivalent defect density is ~4e10 cm-2.

properties.name: defect_type
properties.value: Likely point-like (sp3-type or vacancy-type) defects. Grain or edge boundaries are not favoured but cannot be excluded. D' is not resolved, so ID/ID' is only bounded at ≳5.
properties.source: Eckmann et al., Nano Lett. 12, 3925 (2012): ID/ID' ≈ 13 for sp3, ≈ 7 for vacancies, ≈ 3.5 for boundaries

properties.name: doping_type
properties.value: not determinable; low/moderate doping at most
properties.source: G is not blue-shifted (1581 cm-1), G FWHM is ~14 cm-1, and I2D/IG is high. Das et al., Nat. Nanotechnol. 3, 210 (2008)

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.source: The 2D position (2699 cm-1) is higher than the usual ~2680 cm-1 for neutral graphene at 532 nm, but G is not up-shifted. Strain and doping cannot be separated without a calibrated reference or a Pos(G)–Pos(2D) vector analysis (Lee et al., Nat. Commun. 3, 1024 (2012)).

properties.name: background
properties.value: Broad smooth hump, ~2.2–3.3k counts at 1100–1700 cm-1 falling to ~1.2–1.4k at 2500–3000 cm-1
properties.source: Median-binned intensity. Likely a luminescence or substrate background.

artifacts.type: Smooth broad luminescence/substrate background hump, subtracted locally in the fits
Noise ripples at ~1178 and ~1249 cm-1 (only ~200–300 counts above the local level, comparable to the ~100-count noise). They are not reproducible features and were not assigned.
Isolated noise point at ~2039 cm-1, not a real peak
No cosmic-ray spikes were identified among the reported peaks

citations: Ferrari et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 187401 (2006)
limits: L_D is a rough estimate. It assumes point-like defects, a single 532 nm excitation and the Cançado calibration, and it ignores the baseline-subtraction uncertainty and any doping dependence of the intensities. Treat it as ±~30%.
The D' band (~1620 cm-1) is not resolved above the noise (~100 counts), so only ID/ID' ≳ 5 follows. The defect type is therefore a tentative inference. D+D' (~2950 cm-1) is also absent.
The 2D position (2699 cm-1) is unusually high for neutral graphene at 532 nm. Doping and strain cannot be separated from one spectrum, so I report neither sign.
Si 520.7 cm-1 and the other Si/SiO2 lines are outside the 1100–3000 cm-1 window. The substrate is therefore not confirmed spectroscopically and is taken from the metadata.
The data say nothing about the stacking order beyond the single-Lorentzian 2D. They also cannot give lateral uniformity, since this is a single spectrum, or the polarization behaviour.
The broad background was not characterized. Its origin (PL, fluorescence or substrate) is unknown.
The D intensity could also include a contribution from edges or grain boundaries if the laser spot is near one.
